unhomed_statement_fields.standalone: The claim restated with enough context to judge it cold. `title` is the short form and `description` is taken by the quote anchor.
unhomed_statement_fields.attribution: Whether the paper is reporting its own result or somebody else's. Without this axis, 'who first showed X' returns the most recent repeater. Nobody has proposed it upstream; it is the strongest of ours.
unhomed_statement_fields.confidence_class: Whether a record was read off the source, inferred, or ambiguous. MIRA already imports PROV, so this may need a convention rather than a slot.
unhomed_statement_fields.extraction_method: Which model drafted a record, under which brief, on what date. `creator` carries an account standing for the drafter, which is where MIRA's own extractor puts it, but the brief and the date of the reading have nowhere to go.
unhomed_statement_fields.review_status / reviewed_by / verdict /: Who checked this against the paper and what they concluded. RRGI has proposed endorsements upstream (schema PR #32); an author's verdict counting differently from a reader's is the part still missing.
unhomed_statement_fields.concept_tags: Proposed upstream by RRGI as contextEntities (schema issue #35).
unhomed_statement_fields.entity_ids: The named things a statement is about — a system, an organization, a particular deployment. Designed here and not yet built; see docs/concepts-and-entities.md for why these are not concepts.

notes: 103 topic nodes: Taxonomy sections. RRGI has proposed tradition/stemsFrom upstream.
62 concept nodes: Concept tags. RRGI has proposed contextEntities upstream.

15 records are not documents — tools, deployments and evaluation suites, held as records so a statement can point at one. MIRA's SourceDocument is_a CreativeWork and would be a false description of them. A class for a studied artefact is one of ours to propose.

A statement that is not a finding reaches its paper only through the anchor Item's container, by URI convention. MIRA has no slot from a Claim to the document that asserts it, which is the single largest thing this projection cannot say.
MIRA's Question carries no slots of its own. The reasoning for a cluster is emitted as `content`; who asserted it and when, and the question's status, have nowhere to go.

112 MAKES_CLAIM edges: MIRA routes a document to a claim through Study and Evidence. We have no Study nodes, so this is carried by the anchor convention instead: a claim's quote is an Item in the paper's Container.
581 CITES edges: Citation between documents is outside MIRA's scope; dcterms:references would serve but is not in its context.
719 SIMILAR_TO edges: Computed bibliographic coupling. Ours alone.
344 TAGGED_WITH edges: Concept tags. RRGI has proposed the same thing upstream as contextEntities (schema issue #35).
185 ABOUT edges: Taxonomy placement. RRGI has proposed the same thing upstream as tradition/stemsFrom (schema issue #35).
87 PARENT_OF edges: Taxonomy hierarchy. Ours alone.
2 byline pairs differ only in punctuation and were emitted as one account: 'Joon Sung Park'/'Joon-Sung Park'; 'Sheer El-Showk'/'Sheer El Showk'. Worth fixing in the corpus rather than only here.
